name: Department of War Office of Strategic Capital (OSC)
rationale: The specific sub-agency vehicle that actually signs the loan commitments recorded this week (Sila Nanotechnologies $1.4bn, Sunrise Energy Metals $400m, Niron Magnetics $150m - all 7 Aug 2026). Per its own reporting, OSC has committed >$8.4bn in debt financing and mobilized >$17.8bn in total capital from public and private sectors in FY26 alone. Tracking OSC as a named vehicle (parallel to how the CHIPS R&D Office sits inside Commerce) would let a future run trace its pipeline directly rather than rediscovering it deal-by-deal via White House fact sheets.

name: HUMAIN Ventures
rationale: The venture-investing arm of HUMAIN (PIF's wholly-owned AI vehicle, itself flagged in runs/2026-W32/sovereigns/discovered_allocators.csv). Made its first-ever investment in a Saudi company (MOZN, 3 Aug 2026) this week - a smaller, application-layer bet distinct from HUMAIN's large infrastructure/compute deals (AirTrunk, Cohere, xAI). Worth tracking separately since it signals PIF/HUMAIN capital reaching into the AI-applications layer, not just datacenters and frontier labs.
